library(nnet)
library(caret)

Load Data


df <- read_csv('game_teams_stats.csv')

Rows: 52610 Columns: 17
── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Delimiter: ","
chr  (4): HoA, settled_in, head_coach, startRinkSide
dbl (12): game_id, team_id, goals, shots, hits, pim, powerPlayOpportunities,...
lgl  (1): won

ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.
ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.



Make Necessary Adjustments for Nominal Response Target Bin goals into nominal categories: ‘Low’ (0-1), ‘Medium’ (2-3), ‘High’ (4+)


df <- df %>%
mutate(
goals_nominal = case_when(
goals <= 1 ~ "Low_Goals",
goals <= 3 ~ "Medium_Goals",
TRUE ~ "High_Goals"
),
goals_nominal = as.factor(goals_nominal)
)


Feature Selection & Data Cleaning Drop target leakage (‘won’, ‘powerPlayGoals’), raw ‘goals’, and IDs


leakage_cols <- c("goals", "won", "powerPlayGoals", "game_id", "team_id", "head_coach")
df_model <- df %>%
select(-any_of(leakage_cols)) %>%
mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor)) %>%
drop_na()


Train/Test Split (Stratified by goals_nominal)


train_index <- createDataPartition(df_model$goals_nominal, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_data <- df_model[train_index, ]
test_data <- df_model[-train_index, ]

set.seed(42)

Set the Reference Level for the Nominal Factor ‘Low_Goals’ will serve as the baseline category for the log-odds comparisons


train_data$goals_nominal <- relevel(train_data$goals_nominal, ref = "Low_Goals")
test_data$goals_nominal <- relevel(test_data$goals_nominal, ref = "Low_Goals")


Fit Multinomial Logistic Regression Model using nnet::multinom Note: scaling numeric predictors beforehand can help convergence if scales differ vastly


model <- multinom(goals_nominal ~ ., data = train_data, MaxNWts = 2000)

title: AI Use
text:
AI Check 1
During AI given model correctly looks at the goals as ordinal values. By turning them into catagorical values. I would be cautious looking at the data, because of the way the values are just being dropped. By just dropping the data it might affect the model and the predictions there needs to be a different way to clean the data.

title: AI Use
text:
AI Check 2
The goals are already somewhat ordinal, so maybe they just need to be ordered and catagorized. Then the predictors aren’t scaled accurately all of the variables have different ranges and values and need to be standardized.

title: Case Study
text: One of the most popular professional sports in Canada and the United states is Ice Hockey. Hockey brings excitment and goal scoring to the ice. In every game there are a handfull of goals that determine who wins the game. In this study we look at what factors contribute to total goals scored by a team in a game. Some of the factors that we will be looking at include power play opprotunities, shots on goal, shots blocked, home or away, and others. By looking at what factors are associated with more goals being it scored it will help teams to know what they need to focus on in order to score more goals. It also can help managers, fans, and even brodcasting networks know which games will have characteristics associated with more goals being scored. All of thsi data will help give more information and imporve the game adn entertainment vaule of hockey.

title: Case Study
text:
Research Questions
How do much do different factors in a game contribute to the amount of goals scored in an NHL game, leading to the higher scoring game? How well can we predict how many goals are scored based off of a model to predict goals scored by a team in a game based off of the factors we studied?

title: Case Study
text:
About Data
The data was collected by using Kevin Sidwar’s “documenting the still un-documented NHL stats API”. There was no licisnceing that was found on kaggle when the data was collected and all of the information on here is public knowledge and could be found if you took the time your self. I don’t think there is any privacy or ethical concerns with this dataset. The data includes scores and measured statistics from NHL games over many years. Some of the measured statistics include the amount of goals scored, the amount of shots, which teams were home or away, the amount of power play opprotunities and many other commonly measured hockey statistics.
